thread:
maria (runtime): Ran a new attention sweep across A100/H100/L40S this morning. hitting a weird latency kink on L40S at seq=2048 bsz=8, p99 way above expected. anyone seen this pattern?

ashwin: ugh. can you paste the perf-bot output? which kernel variant got chosen? :eyes:

maria (runtime): perf-bot attached below. weird thing is kernel_selector picked fused_paged_opt but runtime fell back to a flash-ish path midway through token generation.

perf-bot: ```
run_id: 2026-03-17-07
target: L40S
model: rwd-small-attn (2B)
seq: 64, 256, 1024, 2048
bsz sweep: 1,4,8,16
At seq=2048, bsz=8:
  selected_kernel: fused_paged_opt_v3
  runtime_path: fused_paged_opt_v3 -> fallback -> flash_variant_x
  p50: 28.1ms p95: 67.3ms p99: 112.6ms (expected p99 ~ 55ms)
  kv_cache_hits: 86%
  mem_spill_events: 4
  trace_id: tf-4123456789
```

kevin: mem_spill_events=4 looks suspicious. did the eviction window align badly with our prefetch heuristic?

maria (runtime): i thought prefetch window should avoid spills at this bsz/seq. prefetch config for this run: `prefetch_steps=2, prefetch_tokens=1024, kv_warm_threshold=0.7`

ashwin: can you repro with trace enabled and capture kernel selection logs + allocator timeline? small script:```
./bench_tool --gpu L40S --model rwd-small-attn --seq 2048 --bsz 8 --trace kernel,allocator --out /tmp/trace.json
```

maria (runtime): started a repro now, uploading trace. in the meantime i dumped selected kernels vs step index. looks like at token ~320 the selector flips to flash_variant_x even though fused_paged_opt had better historical perf for this sequence length.

sasha: @maria can you confirm the model tokenization pattern? long prefixes with many repeated tokens can change kv cache effectiveness and heat the eviction policy.

maria (runtime): good call. this trace uses long-system prompt (~800 tokens) + generation 1248 tokens. so initial prefix warm-up is heavy. kv_cache hit% starts ~95% and drops to 82% during generation.

bench-bot: quick compare across GPUs (same model+prompt):
- A100 seq=2048 bsz=8 p99=58ms kernel=flash_variant_x stable
- H100 seq=2048 bsz=8 p99=61ms kernel=fused_paged_opt_v3 stable
- L40S seq=2048 bsz=8 p99=112ms kernel=flash_variant_x fallback events present

kevin: L40S memory bank layout + our memcpy microkernel might be thrashing when we cross page boundaries for 2048 seq + bsz 8. fallback could be due to a kernel failure (timeout) or due to out-of-register heuristics. any kernel logs?

maria (runtime): kernel logs show one kernel returned CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_TIMEOUT? but we run in non-display mode; maybe kernel got caught by watchdog on L40S due to longer kernel runtime after a memcpy stall. partial logs:
```
[trace] step=319 kernel=fused_paged_opt_v3 start=0x7f.. dur=78ms status=ok
[trace] step=320 kernel=fused_paged_opt_v3 start=0x7f.. dur=340ms status=warn memcpy_wait
[trace] step=321 kernel=flash_variant_x start=0x7f.. dur=95ms status=ok
```

ashwin: memcpy_wait indicates DMA contention. were there concurrent copies or interleaved host pinned-buffer operations at that time?

maria (runtime): scheduler snapshot shows a background eviction daemon kicked around that time copying cold KV shards to disk. It's supposed to be low-priority but maybe IO stalled GPU page migration?

kevin: that's the key. if eviction kicks during the critical token window, our kernel might stall waiting for page residency, causing a long-running kernel path and then selector fallbacks. we should ensure eviction uses a pinned-async copy queue that doesn't block compute streams.

sasha: also worth checking batch boundary alignment. our batching heuristic will combine short requests into B=8; if a long request with seq tail interacts with 7 short ones, memory layout for KV can fragment.

maria (runtime): I ran a targeted run disabling eviction during run and forcing pinned async copies. result: L40S seq=2048 bsz=8 p99 dropped to 62ms, kernel stayed fused_paged_opt_v3 throughout.

ashwin: nice. so two mitigations: (1) change eviction to use async pinned copies and postpone heavy IO during active generation windows, (2) tweak kernel_selector to prefer stable kernels if recent memcpy_wait warnings observed.

kevin: we should also add a small hysteresis in selector: avoid switching kernels for N tokens after a long-running memcpy or an eviction event. reduce flip-flop.

maria (runtime): agreed. i'll open a PR with:
- eviction: use cudaMemcpyAsync with pinned staging, elastic backoff during active gen windows
- selector: add hysteresis window of 512 tokens after memcpy_wait or mem_spill event
- batching: prefer grouping requests by estimated seq length to reduce fragmentation

maria (runtime): PR draft: https://git.internal/rwd/inference/pulls/8012 (WIP)

bench-bot: after local patch applied in staging, quick sweep: L40S seq sweep results
- seq=1024 bsz=8 p99=38ms
- seq=2048 bsz=8 p99=61ms (no fallback)
- seq=4096 bsz=4 p99=220ms (expected higher)

sasha: can we add an instrumentation counter for "selector flips per trace" and alert if flips > 3 per trace? that's a useful signal for instability.

maria (runtime): good idea. i'll add that metric and a tiny dashboard tile in console.

ashwin: quick note: ensure change is behind opt-in flag for Dedicated customers until we've verified stability across multi-tenant workloads.

maria (runtime): yes will gate with `runtime.eviction.async_pinned=true` and `runtime.selector.hysteresis_tokens=512` flags. Rolling test on staging for 24h.

kevin: add a unit test that simulates eviction during active generation and asserts no kernel launch stalls. can mock the memcpy delays.

maria (runtime): will do. thanks all. summary: root cause likely eviction-triggered memcpy stalls causing kernel slowdown -> selector flips -> p99 spike on L40S for certain seq/bsz combos. mitigation implemented: async pinned eviction + selector hysteresis + batching alignment. follow-up: check production metrics after flag rollout next week. :thumbsup:
